title: Research
text:
My work sits at the intersection of assistive robotics and physical human-robot interaction: designing sensor-driven systems that infer what a person intends to do — from a gait mode to a sit-to-stand transition — and turning that inference into safe, adaptive robotic assistance in real time.
Keywords: Wearable Robotics · Assistive Robotics · Multimodal Learning · Nonlinear Control

title: Research
text:
Professional Experience



Jul 2026 – Present


Postdoctoral Researcher

Université Paris-Est Créteil, Vitry-sur-Seine, France


Designed a high-precision gait mode recognition system using LSTM networks, achieving 98% classification accuracy and enabling real-time intent detection for actuated ankle-foot orthoses.
Developed an energy-efficient adaptive FES control strategy based on surface EMG signals, reducing stimulation energy consumption by 30% while significantly mitigating muscle fatigue in clinical trials.
Implemented a multi-sensor fusion framework (7 IMUs) to extract kinematic metrics for lower-limb joint analysis and Parkinson’s disease diagnosis in a portable clinical device.

title: Huiseok Moon
text:
Research Interests
My research combines Assistive Robotics and Physical Human-Robot Interaction, building on my experience designing clinically validated real-time intent detection frameworks and assistive robotic control based on sensor systems (EMG, IMU, etc.). I am interested in physics-based modeling and simulation, model-based control, and multimodal AI for understanding and predicting human motion — with a focus on mobility assistance for wearable robotics.


Wearable Robotics
Actuated ankle-foot orthoses and lower-limb exoskeletons for gait and mobility assistance.


Assistive & Adaptive Control
Impedance control, funnel-based and fuzzy-adaptive control for human-exoskeleton interaction.


Multimodal Learning
LSTM / GRU / attention-based models fusing EMG, IMU, and FSR signals for intent and gait recognition.


Nonlinear & Model-Based Control
Physics-based modeling and model predictive / reference-tracking control for rehabilitation robots.

title: About
text:
I’m Huiseok Moon, a postdoctoral researcher at Université Paris-Est Créteil (LISSI), working on assistive robotics and physical human-robot interaction. My path has taken me through mechanical engineering (Sogang University), robotics (Kwangwoon University), and a Ph.D. on human-in-the-loop mobility assistance (UPEC), with a postdoctoral stay at KAIST along the way.
I like building systems that sit at the boundary between a person and a machine — where a control law has to be both precise and forgiving, and where a model has to explain a limp, a hesitation, or a stumble in time to help.
